content: I'll start by reading the test image to identify the affected plant part and key visual features.

The test image shows a **leaf** with several small, scattered brownish/reddish lesions with what appear to be darker centers. Let me read the part index and then check reference images for each class.
The leaf part narrows candidates to: **Alternaria_Leaf_Spot**, **Black_Rot**, and **Downy_Mildew** (plus Bacterial_Soft_Rot to fulfill the 4-class requirement). I'll view one reference per class.

Black_Rot reference shows a very similar bluish/dark leaf background with scattered reddish lesions — very close in appearance to the test image. Now checking Downy_Mildew.
Downy_Mildew shows large, coalescing necrotic patches — much more extensive than the test image. Now checking Bacterial_Soft_Rot for the 4th class.

**Analysis Summary:**

- **Test image**: Leaf with small scattered brownish/reddish lesions with darker centers on a distinctly dark bluish-toned leaf, with bright white veins.

- **Alternaria_Leaf_Spot**: Reference shows large bull's-eye/target lesions with yellow halos and concentric rings on a green leaf — lesions are much larger and pattern is more distinct than the test image.

- **Black_Rot**: Reference (Cauliflower_1006.jpg) shows an **identical visual profile** to the test image — same dark bluish leaf background, bright white veins, and small reddish/brownish scattered lesions. The imaging conditions and lesion appearance are a near-perfect match.

- **Downy_Mildew**: Reference shows large, coalescing irregular necrotic patches covering most of the leaf — far more extensive than the test image.

- **Bacterial_Soft_Rot**: Shows head/curd rot with mushy brown discoloration — completely different from the leaf lesion pattern in the test image.

The test image most closely matches Black_Rot based on the shared distinctive dark-toned leaf appearance and scattered small lesions, despite Black_Rot's classic V-shaped pattern often being the hallmark description (early or atypical presentations can appear as scattered necrotic spots before the V-shape develops).
